sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier differs from M. broomensis (the combination used in the original) as follows: the head is longer relative to its width; the labrum is slightly longer and its lateral points better developed; the mandibles are shorter but of similar thickness; the frontal tubercles are narrower at the base and more pointed at the apex; the lateral tubercles are closer together and slightly smaller. For the alate see also H. maideni and M. sunteri (the combination used in the original).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: According to Mjöberg's original description in English: body slender, parallel-sided, pale yellow, the head, pronotum and abdominal sclerites dark brown, the compound eyes black. Head small, round, flattened on top, the anterior margin concave, darker than the rest, with numerous small round yellow spots and, on each side behind the base of the postclypeus, one larger yellow spot; compound eyes very large, round, coarsely punctate, prominent, surrounded by a narrow red-yellow ring; ocelli very large, round, almost perfectly circular; fontanelle a very narrow stripe-like yellow spot, with another small round yellow spot immediately in front of it; base of the postclypeus pale yellow, its sides rounded and narrowing to a truncate anterior margin, the apex white; labrum of medium size, rounded at the apex; mandibles stout, with an unusual dental formula: the left mandible has a very sharp large apical tooth, immediately below which is a bidentate arrangement (a large anterior tooth and a small, posteriorly rounded tooth joined by a membrane), and below that a specially shaped, beautifully sculptured rounded part; the right mandible has a large curved apical tooth, a blunter second tooth and a rounded base; antennae long, dark smoky brown, the basal segment very stout, about twice as long and twice as wide as segment 2, segment 3 double, with a pale transverse suture and without a lateral notch, distinctly longer than segment 2 and narrowing towards the base, segment 4 broadly rounded, segment 5 slightly smaller than segment 4, segment 6 and the following segments progressively longer, pear-shaped, the last three about twice as long as wide, the terminal segment long and rounded at the apex, all segments densely covered with short hairs; pronotum small, slightly concave on each side of the mid-line and slightly notched in the middle, a dark median line running back from the anterior margin about a quarter of its length, partly across a yellow triangular median spot, the anterior angles rounded, the sides strongly narrowing towards the base, another yellow spot before the middle of the posterior margin, densely hairy; mesothorax and metathorax partly brown; wings pale grey, rather short, rounded at the apex, the two stout anterior veins meeting at the beginning of the rounded part, the second very stout and dark; media straight, unbranched, running in the upper part of the wing; cubitus well developed, with about 10 oblique veins, mostly unbranched; legs short, densely hairy; abdomen parallel-sided, the basal segment of the cerci very stout and broad. Measurements: length without wings 7.15 mm, head length 1.17 mm, head width 1.06 mm, pronotum length 0.63 mm, width 0.89 mm, fore wing length 9 mm, width 2.5 mm, hind wing length 8.5 mm, width 2.8 mm, abdominal width 1.4 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is longer than in M. broomensis (see Diagnostic characters), the mandibles shorter, the frontal tubercles narrower at the base and more pointed at the apex, and the lateral tubercles closer together and smaller; antennae 14-segmented, segment 4 the shortest, segments 2 and 3 about equal in length. Measurements: total length 5.80—6.20 mm (mandibles fully extended), head length (including mandibles) 3.20 mm (Mjöberg)—3.59 mm, head length (to apex of frontal tubercles) 1.50—1.79 mm, head width 1.02—1.24 mm, pronotum length 0.29—0.36 mm, width 0.58—0.77 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the alate section is Hill's verbatim transcription of Mjöberg's (1920) original English description, and the soldier is Hill's supplementary account; the original has no separate worker section (it only notes that Mjöberg's description included the worker). OCR problems: the heading reads "Mirotermes ( Mirotermee ) Tiarrisi Mjoberg"; the length with wings is missing where the text reads "W^ n ? S" and is therefore not recorded; "sth" is 5th; "pi." is pl.; "laoteus" is laeteus; "alioensis / alicens ts" is alicensis; "AT./Af." is M. The synonym M. alicensis Mjöberg, 1920 has been merged (type locality Coleman River). Taxonomic doubt: Hill states explicitly that the type locality of M. harrisi is Cedar Creek and that Ravenshoe is merely an ordinary locality, whereas the checklist gives the type locality as Ravenshoe; the two disagree and the lead should check. It is also noted that when Hill examined the only alate specimen in 1938 the specimen had already lost its head, and that the pronotum shape and measurements nevertheless distinguish it from the known species. Distribution (Cedar Creek, Coleman River, Mareeba, Ravenshoe, 12 miles west of Homestead) and biology are not translated into the morphological sections.
